### Project Name

AGNTCY

### Project Description

AGNTCY is an open source project building the infrastructure layer for multi-agent systems: how agents are **discovered**, how they **prove who they are**, how they **communicate securely**, and how their behavior is **observed and evaluated**. It comprises four technical components under one governance structure:

- **Agent Directory (dir)** — distributed announce and discovery of MCP servers, A2A servers, Agent Skills and additional AI capabilities for multi-agent systems via their metadata. It levarages OCI as object storage and uses OASF a schema framework. Discovery nodes can share their content using a DHT which allows for network discovery <https://github.com/agntcy/dir>

- **OASF (Open Agentic Schema Framework)** — the record schema that describes MCP servers, A2A servers, Agent-Skills artifacts, and new objects, private, public and experimental. Derived from OCSF (Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework). The core object schema now leverages AI Catalog the team contributed to for interoperability <https://github.com/agntcy/oasf>

- **SLIM (Secure Low-Latency Interactive Messaging)** — It is a multiagent transport protocol which is also an experimental custom protocol binding for A2A. Designed as a multiparty messaging for agent with support for multicast RPC which allows agents (and humans) to collaborate efficiently, coordinate and scale. It is designed as a cloud native transport but also for end devices. Communications in the group are secured using the Messaging Layer Security standard (MLS RFC) while network connections leverage HTTP/2 low latency and scalable transport. <https://github.com/agntcy/slim>

- **Identity** — verifiable credentials and agent badges for agents, MCP servers and multi-agent systems, supporting bring-your-own-identity (IdP-issued IDs, A2A Agent Cards) and W3C DIDs. Support for Tool Based Access Control (TBAC) for granular agent – tool policy controls <https://github.com/agntcy/identity>, spec at <https://spec.identity.agntcy.org/>

- **Observe** — an observability SDK and the Metrics Compute Engine (MCE), extending the OpenTelemetry GenAI/LLM semantic conventions downstream with agent-specific spans and computed output-quality metrics. <https://github.com/agntcy/observe>, <https://github.com/agntcy/telemetry-hub>

- **SHADI (Secure Host for Agentic AI Dynamic Instantiation)** — a secure runtime host for agents, combining identity verification before secret release, OS-level sandboxing of what a process can read, write, execute and reach on the network, encrypted local memory, and authenticated messaging. Components: shadictl (policy, sandbox execution, identity, secrets, memory and shell control), shadi_sandbox (OS-enforced policy), agent_secrets (keychain-backed storage with verification gates), shadi_memory (SQLCipher-backed encrypted memory), and agent_transport_slim (secure transport and stdio bridging). Rust; Apache-2.0. <https://github.com/agntcy/shadi>, docs at <https://agntcy.github.io/shadi>

- **AgentBridge** — a general-purpose agent interconnect over A2A, shipped as a CLI within SHADI. It maps A2A client and server interfaces into an agentic harness in a standard way, with coding CLIs (Claude Code, Copilot, Codex, Cursor Agent) as the flagship use case. Distributed via Homebrew (agntcy/shadi/agentbridge) and WinGet (AGNTCY.agentbridge) alongside shadictl, on independent release tags (agntcy-agentbridge-cli, agntcy-shadi-cli), with prebuilt archives for Linux (x86_64, aarch64), macOS (arm64, x86_64) and Windows (x86_64). <https://agntcy.github.io/shadi/agentbridge/>

- **coffeeAGNTCY** — reference multi-agent application and developer sandbox for enterpries learning, testing, and demonstrating AGNTCY patterns in a working system. Provides reusable agentic patterns, reference implementations, and end-to-end examples across discovery, identity, messaging, observability, and multi-agent coordination. Designed as a practical starting point for enterprises building AGNTCY-based PoCs and validating patterns for procution applications. coffeeAGNTCY is also the reference project being used by the AAIF End User Group (ANDOR) to explore and validate real-world multi-agent use cases and patterns.

**Origin and history.** Cisco open-sourced AGNTCY in March 2025 with LangChain and Galileo. The Linux Foundation [welcomed AGNTCY on 2025-07-29](https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/linux-foundation-welcomes-the-agntcy-project-to-standardize-open-multi-agent-system-infrastructure-and-break-down-ai-agent-silos) with formative members Cisco, Dell Technologies, Google Cloud, Oracle and Red Hat. First commit was 2025-02-05. The project now spans 54 tracked repositories with 406 contributors from 48 organizations ([LFX Insights](https://insights.linuxfoundation.org/project/agntcy), 365-day window, 2026-08-21).

**What we are asking for.** We are requesting that AAIF accept AGNTCY as a hosted project at the **Growth** stage, entering as a whole project in the manner of MCP and A2A, with individual components subsequently aligned to the AAIF working groups that map to them. AGNTCY is already a Linux Foundation project, so this is an intra-foundation transfer: the technical charter, code of conduct, DCO enforcement and trademark custody are already in place under LF Projects, LLC.

**What AGNTCY does not standardize or replace:**

- It does not define how an agent reasons, plans, or is built — no framework, no runtime.

- It does not replace **MCP**; Directory indexes MCP servers and SLIM can carry MCP.

- It does not replace **A2A**; SLIM is a transport binding beneath A2A, and OASF converts to and from A2A Agent Cards.

- It does not replace **agentgateway**; SLIM is an end-to-end transport, not a network-edge proxy.

- It does not replace goose or AGENTS.md. SHADI is a secure host for an agent process, not an agent framework: it decides what a running agent may reach and which secrets it may obtain. A goose agent is the kind of process SHADI is built to host.

- AgentBridge does not extend or alter the A2A specification. It is a client-and-server interconnect built on A2A as it stands, exposing existing harnesses over the protocol.

- It does not define prompt-level guardrails, content filtering, or model evaluation harnesses.

- Observe does not fork OpenTelemetry; it extends the GenAI conventions downstream.

### Alignment with AAIF Mission

Layer | AAIF today | AGNTCY contribution
-- | -- | --
Tool integration | MCP | — (Directory indexes MCP servers)
Agent-to-agent application protocol | A2A | — (SLIM carries A2A)
Network edge mediation | agentgateway | — (complementary)
Agent runtime | goose | —
Capability declaration | AGENTS.md | — (OASF is a machine record, not a human file)
Discovery / registry | none | Directory + OASF
Agent identity | none | Identity
Secure group transport | none | SLIM (MLS, RFC 9420)
Agentic observability semantics | none | Observe + MCE
Agent Sandboxing and secret gating | none | SHADI
Harness interconnect over A2A | none | AgentBridge

AAIF's stated mission is to be the place for developers and companies to build trusted shared technology to accelerate agentic AI adoption and to drive the growth of open-source agentic AI in the broader community. AGNTCY aligns on four specific counts.

**1. It supplies infrastructure layers AAIF does not currently host.** AAIF's five projects cover tools (MCP), agent-to-agent application protocol (A2A), network mediation (agentgateway), an agent runtime (goose), and capability declaration (AGENTS.md). None of them provides agent discovery and registry, agent identity, secure group transport, or agentic observability semantics.

| **Layer** | **AAIF today** | **AGNTCY contribution** |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
| Tool integration | MCP | — (Directory indexes MCP servers) |
| Agent-to-agent application protocol | A2A | — (SLIM carries A2A) |
| Network edge mediation | agentgateway | — (complementary) |
| Agent runtime | goose | — |
| Capability declaration | AGENTS.md | — (OASF is a machine record, not a human file) |
| **Discovery / registry** | **none** | **Directory + OASF** |
| **Agent identity** | **none** | **Identity** |
| **Secure group transport** | **none** | **SLIM (MLS, RFC 9420)** |
| **Agentic observability semantics** | **none** | **Observe + MCE** |
| **Agent Sandboxing and secret gating** | **none** | **SHADI** |
| **Harness interconnect over A2A** | **none** | **AgentBridge** |

**2. It is already load-bearing for an AAIF project.** The A2A proposal accepted by the AAIF Technical Committee ([issue \#37](https://github.com/aaif/project-proposals/issues/37)) cites AGNTCY directly: Cisco "spearheaded the AGNTCY project, compiling A2A over SLIM (Secure Low-Latency Interactive Messaging) to guarantee quantum-safe, end-to-end Message Layer Security (MLS) for autonomous systems in highly regulated sectors." That is AAIF's own characterization. The corresponding code lives inside the A2A organization: [a2aproject/experimental-cpb-slimrpc](https://github.com/a2aproject/experimental-cpb-slimrpc) and [a2aproject/a2a-rs/a2a-slimrpc](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-rs/tree/main/a2a-slimrpc).

**3. It meets AAIF's stated bar on health and neutrality.** [LFX Insights](https://insights.linuxfoundation.org/project/agntcy) rates AGNTCY's Health Score **77— Healthy**, above three of AAIF's five current projects, with 53% quarterly contributor retention and a 3-day median merge lead time. Contributions have been DCO-only since inception, with no CLA.

**4. It is interoperability-first by construction.** OASF converts to and from MCP and A2A formats. Directory indexes MCP servers natively (dirctl mcp serve). SLIM ships bindings for A2A and MCP. Identity accepts A2A Agent Cards and IdP-issued identifiers. Observe extends OpenTelemetry rather than competing with it. AGNTCY's components are only useful if other people's agents work with them, which has kept the design open by necessity rather than by policy.

### Relation to Existing AAIF Projects

**MCP (Anthropic).** Complementary, with active integration. MCP defines how an agent reaches tools; AGNTCY defines how agents and MCP servers are *found*, *trusted*, *reached*, and *observed*. Directory publishes and discovers MCP server records in OASF format and ships an MCP server itself (dirctl mcp serve; [worked example, 2026-02-19](https://blogs.agntcy.org/technical/2026/02/19/directory-mcp-server.html) covering github-mcp, fetch-mcp-server, memory-mcp-server, built on modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk). SLIM provides MCP transports in Python and Rust ([docs](https://slim.agntcy.org/latest/slim/integrations/mcp/)). AGNTCY does not propose changes to the MCP specification.

**A2A (Google).** Complementary, with code already inside the A2A organization. A2A is the application-layer protocol; SLIM is a transport protocol currently made available to A2A v1.0 as custom protocol binding beneath it. The SLIMRPC custom protocol binding (binding ID <https://a2a-protocol.org/bindings/experimental-slimrpc/v1>) lives at [a2aproject/experimental-cpb-slimrpc](https://github.com/a2aproject/experimental-cpb-slimrpc), with the native Rust implementation in [a2aproject/a2a-rs](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-rs/tree/main/a2a-slimrpc) and language bindings implementations in agntcy/slim-a2a-python, -js, -go, -java and -dotnet. AGNTCY maintainers also contribute to A2A directly: Luca Muscariello contributes to A2A as TSC member and as Rust SDK maintainer. Sam Betts contributes as A2A project maintainer. Also A2A TSC and MCP TSC have moved discovery metadata specification into a separate project called AI Catalog and AGNTCY directory maintainers have contributed to the release candidate specification as well as the AI Catalog Rust SDK, Go SDK and the AI Catalog cli (https://github.com/Agent-Card/ai-catalog-rust, https://github.com/Agent-Card/ai-catalog-go https://github.com/Agent-Card/ai-catalog-cli).

**agentgateway ([Solo.io](http://solo.io/)).** Complementary layers, no overlap in function. agentgateway mediates traffic at the network edge — routing, policy, auth at a gateway. SLIM is an end-to-end transport with cryptographic group membership: MLS sessions run between agents, so the gateway is not a trust intermediary. Both are needed for defense in depth, and Cisco is already among agentgateway's named contributing organizations ([LF press release, 2025-08-25](https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press)).

**goose (Block).** No overlap. goose is an agent runtime; AGNTCY is the substrate a runtime would use to discover, authenticate, reach and observe other agents. A goose agent could publish an OASF record to Directory and carry A2A over SLIM, but no such integration exists today.

**AGENTS.md (OpenAI).** No overlap. AGENTS.md is a human-authored file describing how to work in a repository. OASF is a machine-readable record describing a deployed agent's skills and interfaces for discovery. They could compose — an AGENTS.md-aware tool could emit an OASF record — but nothing of the kind is built.

**Relation to adjacent work outside AAIF, for completeness.** OASF derives from OCSF. AGNTCY Directory is one of four reference implementations of Google's [Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD)](https://developers.googleblog.com/announcing-the-agentic-resource-discovery-specification/) specification, announced 2026-06-17 and currently at v0.9 draft; Cisco is a named ARD contributor organization.

### Example Use Cases and Evidence of Adoption

Deployments are labeled by maturity. Two organizations run AGNTCY in production; the remainder are pilots, proofs of concept, lab demonstrations or reference architectures, and are presented as such.

#### **Production deployments**

**1. Splunk — shipping in a generally available commercial product.** Splunk AI Agent Monitoring in Splunk Observability Cloud is built on AGNTCY. From [Splunk's announcement, 2026-06-03](https://www.splunk.com/en_us/blog/observability/monitor-llm-and-agent-performance-with-ai-agent-monitoring-in-splunk-observability-cloud.html): "AI Agent Monitoring is also built on industry standards—OpenTelemetry and Cisco AGNTCY—to provide AI agent monitoring without vendor lock-in," and "Splunk also continues to leverage components of AGNTCY's Metrics Compute Engine to provide advanced quality metrics such as factual accuracy and coherence, and foundational metrics like latency and error rates." GA documentation: [Splunk AI Agent Monitoring](https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-observability-cloud/observability-for-ai/splunk-ai-agent-monitoring). Splunk also contributes to AGNTCY. Collaboration background: [Outshift](https://outshift.cisco.com/blog/how-agntcy-and-splunk-drive-ai-observability).

**2. Cisco Webex — production Agent Central Service.** Per the [Webex Developers Blog, 2026-02-27](https://developer.webex.com/blog/webex-leverages-agntcy-directory-and-identity-for-agentic-apps): "ACS now integrates AGNTCY directory and identity components for registration, discovery, and verification of internal and external MCP servers." Records are stored "in AGNTCY directory service in a standardized Open Agent Schema Framework (OASF) format," and "the AGNTCY identity service is used to issue agent badges during agent app registration and then subsequently to verify the badges upon use." Badge classes are *Cisco Official*, *Cisco Onboarded*, *Developer/partner Onboarded*, and *Federated through external registry*. Agentic apps are listed publicly on [Webex App Hub](https://apphub.webex.com/agentic-apps) with MCP/A2A and Badge Type filters (32 shown on the first page, paginated).

#### **Pilots, proofs of concept and reference architectures**

**ServiceNow — jointly proven reference architecture** (2026-06-09). Outshift and ServiceNow "jointly proven a reference architecture for federated discovery and distributed workflow execution, powered by open standards and the AGNTCY open source stack" ([Outshift](https://outshift.cisco.com/blog/ai-ml/service-now-outshift-multi-agent-enterprise)). Independently characterized by [CIO, 2026-07-27](https://www.cio.com/article/4200144/the-rise-of-the-internet-of-agents-and-why-it-changes-everything.html): It is an early proof point inside the enterprise stack: Agents from different platforms coordinating through a shared layer rather than through brittle, custom integrations." Federated discovery via Directory is verified; ServiceNow is independently a named ARD contributor organization.

**Swisscom — four-month proof of concept** in autonomous network operations, using AGNTCY's observability components to instrument a multi-agent change-validation system ([whitepaper](https://outshift-headless-cms-s3.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/Swisscom%20Whitepaper.pdf), V.1 Oct 2025):

**SoftServe — proof of concept**, multi-agent video intelligence over SLIM and ACP.

**Orium — reproducible reference architecture**, IT incident response. [Orium, 2026-05-12](https://orium.com/blog/multi-agent-incident-response-agntcy):

**Digital Realty — lab demonstration.** coffeeAGNTCY deployed across geographies in the Digital Realty Innovation Lab. coffeeAGNTCY is explicitly "a reference implementation based on a fictitious coffee company."

**Infermedica, Infinitus and Webex — prototype/pilot** healthcare booking multi-agent system exercising Identity, Directory and Observe.

**MACH Alliance.** Outshift is a founding contributor to the MACH Alliance Agent Ecosystem initiative ([MACH Alliance, 2026-06-22](https://machalliance.org/insights-hub/the-infrastructure-problem)). MACH Alliance is itself an AAIF Silver Member.

#### **Ecosystem and usage evidence**

- **Cisco AI Catalog**, the ARD reference deployment built on AGNTCY Directory, serves **4,138 records** across A2A Agents, MCP Servers, Agent Skills and Agent Skill Bundles, Sigstore-signed by agntcy/dir CI (verified 2026-08-21 via <https://ai-catalog.outshift.io/v1/agents?pageSize=1>). Public instance: <https://ai-catalog.outshift.io/>. Hosted Directory: <https://dir.agntcy.org/>

- [**[81 supporting organizations](https://agntcy.org/supporters)**](https://agntcy.org/supporters); **48 contributing organizations** and **406 contributors** per LFX Insights.

- **coffeeAGNTCY**, the end-to-end reference application: 109 stars, 51 forks, 384 merged PRs, 18 contributors, release 0.3.0 (2026-08-10) — exercising SLIM group messaging, App SDK, Observe SDK, Identity Service SDK, Directory and OASF alongside A2A, MCP and LangGraph.

- **Hands-on labs** drawing engineers from Amazon, Workday, Dell, Deutsche Telekom, EY, IBM, Lumen, NEC, Swisscom, TCS, Red Hat, SailPoint, Telefónica, Lyft, Booz Allen Hamilton, Persistent, Presidio and Orium (Nov 2025: 67 attendees; Apr 2026: 60 attendees).

- Peer-reviewed research identifies AGNTCY Agent Badge as an emerging decentralized identity mechanism for agent-to-agent trust, built on W3C DIDs and Verifiable Credentials. <https://www.mdpi.com/1999-5903/18/3/171>

- **AGNTCY is increasingly appearing in independent IETF architecture work** alongside MCP and A2A, with recent IETF drafts explicitly recognizing its Identity layer, Verifiable Credentials and Agent Badges. Its Agent Badge model has also been described in peer-reviewed research, while its cross-domain identity and authorization architecture aligns with active IETF work on CIMD, OAuth, delegation and Verifiable Credentials.

### Governance Model

Governance is centralized in [agntcy/governance](https://github.com/agntcy/governance) and operates under LF Projects, LLC.

- **Charter and operating model:** [OPERATING_MODEL.md](https://github.com/agntcy/governance/blob/main/OPERATING_MODEL.md) — "The AGNTCY Charter & Operating Model." A signed technical charter is also present as CHARTER.pdf.

- **Decision-making** (§4): consensus-seeking with a "minimum discussion period (e.g., 3–5 business days)"; "if no major objections are raised, the proposal is considered accepted." For contested matters the TSC may call a vote: "Simple Majority: Required for most issues; Two-Thirds Majority for fundamental changes or governance modifications."

- **Contributor ladder** (§3.1): Adopter → Contributor → Committer → TSC. Contributors are "nominated by two (2) or more committers"; Committers are "nominated by the AGNTCY Technical Steering Committee." Committer status is expressed in CODEOWNERS and GitHub teams.

- **Working groups:** created by TSC approval under [WORKING-GROUP-PROCESSES.md](https://github.com/agntcy/governance/blob/main/WORKING-GROUP-PROCESSES.md), requiring a charter, at least two nominated leads, and a roadmap, submitted as a PR adding working-groups/\<name\>/CHARTER.md. Current working groups: Core (Directory, SLIM), Observe & Eval, Identity, coffee-app-sdk, Marketing.

- **Contribution terms: DCO only, no CLA.** From [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/agntcy/governance/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): "Across AGNTCY, all new inbound code contributions must be accompanied by a Developer Certificate of Origin, or DCO, sign-off. You must include a sign-off in the commit message of your Pull Request for it to be accepted." This has been the rule since inception; there is no CLA to retire.

- **Code of Conduct:** Contributor Covenant, reporting to <[conduct@agntcy.org](http://conduct@agntcy.org/)>.

### Public-Facing Contribution Process for Specifications

- **Code and schema contributions:** [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/agntcy/governance/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) — fork, PR, DCO sign-off, CI must pass, review routed by CODEOWNERS to the component maintainer team.

- **OASF schema changes:** PRs against [agntcy/oasf](https://github.com/agntcy/oasf); buf-ci enforces protobuf compatibility; the live schema server (<https://schema.oasf.outshift.com/>) publishes each version. Oracle's Agent Spec feature extension entered this way (PR \#334, merged 2025-10-16).

- **SLIM protocol changes:** specification work is public in [agntcy/slim-spec](https://github.com/agntcy/slim-spec), the named venue for draft-mpsb-agntcy-slim. Protocol changes are discussed as issues there before implementation.

- **Cross-component design:** GitHub Discussions (<https://github.com/orgs/agntcy/discussions>) and working-group meetings, held weekly or biweekly for 30–60 minutes on the [LFX calendar](https://zoom-lfx.platform.linuxfoundation.org/meetings/agntcy).

- **New working groups:** the PR-based charter process in WORKING-GROUP-PROCESSES.md; see [PR \#11](https://github.com/agntcy/governance/pull/11) as a worked example.

Community channels: Slack (#agntcy-general, \#wg-core, \#wg-observ-and-eval, \#wg-identity, \#wg-coffee-app-sdk), GitHub Discussions.

### Leadership Team & Decision Process

The TSC above is the decision-making body. Its process is defined in OPERATING_MODEL.md §4 and summarized under Governance Model: consensus-seeking with a 3–5 business-day review window, escalating to a simple-majority TSC vote for contested matters and a two-thirds majority for governance changes. Working groups own day-to-day technical direction within their scope and report to the TSC, which approves their creation and dissolution.

Post-acceptance, we propose the AGNTCY TSC continue as the project's TSC under AAIF, retaining its five-organization composition, with the TSC advising the AAIF Governing Board on project health as the AAIF charter contemplates for technical projects. We will publish the TSC election and rotation mechanism within 90 days.

### Roadmap

**Note on provenance:** AGNTCY has previously planned on a rolling ~3-month working-group horizon, with per-WG GitHub Projects boards and repository milestones (dir v1.7.1 and v1.8 are open). The consolidated 12-month roadmap below is published for the first time in support of this application, in line with the AAIF project lifecycle policy's expectation of a concrete 6–12 month roadmap.

**Months 0–3 — governance and foundation hygiene**

- Publish the TSC election, rotation and expansion mechanism (closes OPERATING_MODEL §3.5).

- Name at least two non-Cisco maintainers to component maintainer teams; target committer nominations from Red Hat, Oracle and Dell contributors with merged work.

- Consolidate security reporting on <[security@agntcy.org](http://security@agntcy.org/)> across all repositories, including app-sdk and coffeeAgntcy.

**Months 3–6 — interoperability and specification maturity**

- Advance the A2A SLIMRPC binding from experimental toward a stable custom protocol binding, in coordination with A2A maintainers.

- OASF: complete MCP and A2A round-trip conversion coverage with a public conformance suite

- Directory: track ARD as the specification stabilizes past v0.9; maintain the reference implementation.

- Identity: publish a conformance profile for agent badge issuance and verification.

- Seek IETF working-group engagement for the SLIM drafts.

**Months 6–12 — scale and stage exit**

- Demonstrate two additional production deployments in organizations outside Cisco.

- Achieve organizational contribution diversity sufficient to clear the LFX "Organization Dependency" flag, or publish a transparent account of why it has not moved.

- Align each component with its AAIF working group; complete phased onboarding of all four components.

- Present quarterly updates to the AAIF Technical Committee as the lifecycle policy requires, and prepare the Growth-to-Impact assessment.

### Security


- **Vulnerability reporting:** private disclosure to <[security@agntcy.org](http://security@agntcy.org/)>, coordinated through GitHub Security Advisories, with fixes announced in release notes. SECURITY.md is present in dir, slim, oasf, identity, identity-service, observe, app-sdk and coffeeAgntcy; the Identity repositories commit to a three-business-day acknowledgement. **Disclosed inconsistency:** app-sdk and coffeeAgntcy currently direct reports to <[oss-security@cisco.com](http://oss-security@cisco.com/)>; this will be consolidated on the project alias within 90 days.

- **Automated scanning in the default path:** CodeQL SAST on dir, slim and oasf; container security scanning on dir, slim and oasf; dependency review on the Identity and Observe repositories; buf-ci protobuf compatibility gates on dir, slim and oasf.

- **Supply chain:** Directory records published to the Cisco AI Catalog are Sigstore-signed by agntcy/dir CI (.github/workflows/import-records.yaml). Container images are published to GHCR.

- **Security-relevant design:** SLIM implements MLS (RFC 9420) via mls-rs for end-to-end group messaging with forward secrecy and post-compromise security, over rustls/aws-lc-rs, with SPIFFE support for workload identity. dir uses SPIFFE and Casbin for authorization. ml-kem is present in the SLIM dependency set.

- **OpenSSF assessments.** Four components publish continuously-updated OpenSSF Scorecards, and three hold OpenSSF Best Practices badges at the Passing level:

| **Component** | **Scorecard** | **Run date** | **OpenSSF Best Practices badge** |
| ----------------- | --------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| SHADI | **9.3 / 10** | 2026-09-22 | Passing |
| SLIM | **9.2 / 10** | 2026-09-22 | Silver |
| Agent Directory | **8.6 / 10** | 2026-09-22 | Passing |
| OASF | **9.1 / 10** | 2026-09-19 | Passing  |
| coffeeAgntcy | **8.5 / 10** | 2026-09-23 | Passing |

- All four score 10/10 on Security-Policy, License, Code-Review (9 on SLIM), CI-Tests, Maintained, Binary-Artifacts, Dangerous-Workflow and Dependency-Update-Tool (Renovate), and 10/10 on SAST via CodeQL (9 on SLIM). SLIM and SHADI are fuzzed — SHADI carries eleven cargo-fuzz targets across its sandbox, secrets, identity and AgentBridge crates — and SHADI pins 100% of its 90 CI action dependencies. SLIM scores 10/10 on Signed-Releases with build provenance; Directory signs release artifacts with Sigstore.
